description: Canonical structure of the IA (LLM) tray/menubar submenu, shared by the Windows renderer (windows/ui/menu/menu_llm/menu_main.ahk: LLM_Menu_Build) and the macOS renderer (macos/ui/menu/menu_llm/init.lua: build_item). This is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the ordered settings-row list and the disabled-when-off policy, so the two menus can never drift again (a greying mismatch between them is the exact bug this file prevents). Both renderers iterate `rows` in order and apply `disabled_when_off`. Each row's id maps to a platform builder that fills the submenu and computes the (state-dependent) label — those stay native because they reference platform state (Win32 Menu vs hs menu tables). Validate with tools/test or the per-platform meta tests (windows tests/meta/test_llm_menu_layout_shared.ahk, macos tests/test_llm_menu_layout_shared.lua).

notes.toggle: The enable/disable toggle is NOT a `rows` entry because its representation is platform-specific: macOS renders the parent 'IA' menubar item itself as the toggle (checked = enabled, click = toggle); Windows cannot make a tray submenu parent clickable, so it renders a dedicated toggle row at the TOP of the submenu via AddCategoryToggleItem. Both honour the same enabled state.
notes.disabled_when_off: true  -> the row is greyed while the feature is OFF (a settings knob that is meaningless until predictions run). false -> the row stays usable while OFF so the user can configure it BEFORE enabling (backend + model pickers). macOS expresses the same policy as `disabled = is_disabled or nil` (off OR paused) vs `disabled = paused or nil` (paused only).
notes.platform_only_rows: Some rows are conditional/platform-specific and intentionally NOT in this list: the Ollama 'not installed' warning row (Windows), the API-entries row (macOS, when backend=api — Windows folds API entries inside the model builder), the thinking-model info row (both, conditional on the active model), the inline reset rows (both, conditional on value != default), and the About row (Windows). They are inserted by native code at the documented anchors and do not affect the shared order below.
